title.value: Amyloid-Related Imaging Abnormalities in 2 Phase 3 Studies Evaluating Aducanumab in Patients With Early Alzheimer Disease
title.quote: Amyloid-Related Imaging Abnormalities in 2 Phase 3 Studies Evaluating Aducanumab in Patients With Early Alzheimer Disease

design.value: secondary analysis of 2 double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 randomized clinical trials
design.quote: Secondary analysis of data from the EMERGE and ENGAGE trials, which were 2 double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 randomized clinical trials

n.quote: The combined studies consisted of a total of 3285 participants with Alzheimer disease

population.value: individuals aged 50 to 85 years who met clinical criteria for mild cognitive impairment due to AD or mild dementia due to AD
population.quote: individuals aged 50 to 85 years who met clinical criteria for mild cognitive impairment due to AD or mild dementia due to AD, with amyloid pathology confirmed by visual assessment of amyloid positron emission tomography.

biomarker_confirmation.value: visual assessment of amyloid positron emission tomography
biomarker_confirmation.quote: amyloid pathology confirmed by visual assessment of amyloid positron emission tomography.

comparator.quote: participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to high-dose or low-dose intravenous aducanumab or placebo

followup.value: 76 weeks for a total of 20 doses
followup.quote: monthly intravenous doses over 76 weeks for a total of 20 doses

n_description.value: participants with Alzheimer disease who received 1 or more doses of placebo or aducanumab
n_description.quote: participants with Alzheimer disease who received 1 or more doses of placebo (n = 1087) or aducanumab (n = 2198; 2752 total person-years of exposure) during the placebo-controlled period.

outcomes.name: ARIA-E
outcomes.quote: ARIA-edema (ARIA-E) was the most common adverse event (362 of 1029 [35.2%])
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Most of the secondary analyses for this report were prespecified for the integrated summary of safety

primary_endpoint_status.quote: The primary analysis will be reported elsewhere.
primary_endpoint_status.explanation: This document is a secondary analysis focused on safety (ARIA) and explicitly states that the primary efficacy analysis is reported in a different publication.

harms.name: ARIA-E
harms.quote: ARIA-edema (ARIA-E) was the most common adverse event (362 of 1029 [35.2%])

harms.name: ARIA-E
harms.quote: In the placebo group, 29 of 1076 participants (2.7%) had ARIA-E

harms.name: ARIA-E
harms.quote: incidence of ARIA-E was highest in ApoE ε4 carriers (290 of 674 [43.0%])

harms.name: ARIA-E
harms.quote: vs noncarriers (72 of 355 [20.3%]) in the 10-mg/kg group.

harms.name: ARIA-microhemorrhage
harms.quote: ARIA-microhemorrhage and ARIA–superficial siderosis occurred in 197 participants (19.1%) and 151 participants (14.7%), respectively.

harms.name: Brain microhemorrhages
harms.quote: Brain microhemorrhages were the most common type of ARIA-H (placebo group: 71 [6.6%]; 10-mg/kg group: 197 [19.1%])

harms.name: symptomatic ARIA-E
harms.quote: Of the 362 participants with ARIA-E in the 10-mg/kg group, 94 (26.0%) were symptomatic

harms.name: Hemorrhage >1 cm
harms.quote: Larger brain hemorrhages measuring more than 1 cm in diameter were rare and balanced between placebo and aducanumab groups (placebo group: 4 [0.4%]; 10-mg/kg group: 3 [0.3%]).

harms.name: Hemorrhage >1 cm
harms.quote: Larger brain hemorrhages measuring more than 1 cm in diameter were rare and balanced between placebo and aducanumab groups (placebo group: 4 [0.4%]; 10-mg/kg group: 3 [0.3%]).

harms.name: deaths due to ARIA
harms.quote: There were no deaths due to ARIA.

deaths.quote: There were no deaths due to ARIA.

discontinuations.value: 64 participants (6.2%) discontinued treatment due to ARIA
discontinuations.quote: Overall, 64 participants (6.2%) discontinued treatment due to ARIA.

limitations: early termination of the trials (35% of participants in the EMERGE trial and 30% in the ENGAGE trial withdrew owing to early study termination), which led to fewer patients completing a full course of dosing and could potentially impact the incidence of adverse events.
the global phase 3 study populations lacked racial and ethnic diversity; therefore, very limited data about the frequency and severity of ARIA in diverse populations are available.
Data are not available for initiation of treatment at other stages of disease (ie, preclinical) or later (ie, moderate to severe dementia) stages of AD

risk_of_bias.judgement: High attrition due to early study termination by the sponsor
risk_of_bias.quote: early termination of the trials (35% of participants in the EMERGE trial and 30% in the ENGAGE trial withdrew owing to early study termination), which led to fewer patients completing a full course of dosing and could potentially impact the incidence of adverse events.
